title: Getters, Setters, and Attribute Helpers
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of getters, setters, and attribute helpers in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply getters, setters, and attribute helpers in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to when explicit methods are preferable and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Getters, Setters, and Attribute Helpers through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding getters, setters, and attribute helpers helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Getters, Setters, and Attribute Helpers helps you reason about attr_reader. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: attr_reader. Then connect it to attr_writer. The remaining syllabus points—attr_accessor, When explicit methods are preferable—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Getters, Setters, and Attribute Helpers
content_blocks.code:
class Book
  attr_reader :title
  def initialize(title)
    @title = title
  end
end
puts Book.new("Ruby Basics").title

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports getters, setters, and attribute helpers. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for getters, setters, and attribute helpers using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (When explicit methods are preferable), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain getters, setters, and attribute helpers, identify its place in object-oriented programming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
